_doc: THE ENSEMBLE — this piece's parts as notation data (the port, PLAN 0g, 2026-09-17; the shape and every mechanism are piece #5's, its PLAN 2a.1–2a.3). Indexed by the composer score's LAYER, which is the IR's `part`. Read by layout.js (clef, written pitch, staves), render.js (part labels, brackets, brace), the notation app and the exports (lane weights, the frame's parts). Everything here is piece data: the engine knows clefs, transpositions and staves, not english horns. A caller that passes no ensemble gets the tuba piece's behaviour exactly — ten bass-clef lanes labelled T1..T10 — which is how the inherited batteries stay green.
_check: tools/notate_section.js refuses to extract when a part's `id` or `short` differs from the score's tracks[part] — the registry cannot drift from the composer score silently. The ids and shorts below are composer.html's TRACKS exactly; tools/palette_check.js guards the other direction.
_layersNote: composer.html: META_LAYER = 8 (= tracks.length), CURVE_LAYERS = [9, 10, 11] (the curve windows A/B/C, over the last three lanes — Vibraphone · Cello · D. Bass). Neither is a part; the extractor's default parts are 0..tracks.length-1. EIGHT parts since 2026-09-18 (D12): the bowed vibraphone took lane 5 and everything below moved one down; a layoutVersion 6 save is migrated in composer.html restoreData.
_transposeConvention: WRITTEN = SOUNDING + transpose semitones (layout.js line 75, and applied at line 965 — read in the code, not taken from a comment, during the port). The IR is always SOUNDING pitch (#5's D9); the shift happens at layout only, and the note is spelled from the written pitch. Piece #5's bass clarinet (+14, written a major ninth above sounding) is the precedent that fixes the sign.

parts._transposeNote: In F: sounds a perfect fifth BELOW written, so the part is written a fifth above sounding = +7. Its library is not yet chosen (journal D6), but the transposition is a property of the instrument, not of the sample library.

parts._clefNote: IRCAM Solo Instruments 2 manual: "Instrument part to be written at actual pitch" — no transposition. Bass clef; the TENOR clef a bassoon part normally takes in its upper register is on the 2a list (the engine draws treble, alto and bass today).

parts._transposeNote: In F. The SI2 manual says it outright: "Instrument part to be written a perfect fifth higher" — read from the manual during the port, not from memory. Sounding range B1–F4.

SI2's trumpet is in C and its manual says "written at actual pitch", so no transposition. WHETHER THE PART IS WRITTEN IN C OR IN B♭ IS THE COMPOSER'S CALL (2a) — a B♭ part is transpose 2, and the library is unaffected either way.

parts._clefNote: PLACEHOLDER still, but narrower than it was: the fourteen ARO instruments are chosen and mapped (LG-10, RUNNING_LOG §37–§42) and they are all SMALL METALS and other unpitched percussion, so this lane wants percussion notation proper — a percussion clef, one-line and five-line staff types, unpitched noteheads — which is on the 2a list. Treble is what the engine can draw today. The bowed vibraphone is NO LONGER in this lane: it took part 5 at his word on 2026-09-18 (D12) because the opening sustains it continuously (LG-15). Same PLAYER, two parts.

SINGLE staff, treble clef, and NO transposition — the standard for vibraphone and confirmed by him 2026-09-18. Range F3–F6 sounding (MIDI 53–89), which sits inside treble with a few ledger lines at the bottom; a grand staff belongs to the marimba, not here, and LG-15's two overlapping pitches read better as a dyad on one staff than split across two. Played by the PERCUSSIONIST (part 4's player), which is why parts 4 and 5 are joined by a brace rather than a bracket.
As piece #5. Tenor clef for the upper register is on the 2a list.

parts._transposeNote: The double bass sounds an OCTAVE BELOW its written part, so written = sounding + 12. The IR holds the sounding pitch (E1 = 28 upward); the staff shows it an octave higher, which is what a player expects.

_groupsNote: Orchestral score order, top to bottom (#5's D10), which also puts the composer's three PAIRS (his note of 2026-09-04, COMPOSITION_NOTES LG-1) in their own brackets: english horn + bassoon · horn + trumpet · cello + double bass. The percussionist sits between the brass and the strings and now holds TWO parts — 4 Percussion and 5 Vibraphone — joined by a BRACE, which is the standard mark for several staves belonging to one player (2026-09-18, D12). It is not a bracket: a bracket means a section, and there is still one percussionist. No grand staff anywhere in the piece.
